decision.actionLabel: Confirm the electrician's proposed 29 September visit (after 15:00), ask for an arrival window and set the scope limits for the TV and the light
decision.message:
Hi Rian,

Thank you for proposing Monday 29 September after 15:00 for 8 Vellum Court, Brindlewick, ZZ1 1ZZ. The tenant offered that slot, so please go ahead and book it. We are asking the tenant to confirm it today as well.

Please could you:
1. Reply by Friday 19 September with an arrival window for the 29th (for example 15:00–17:00) and written confirmation of the booking.
2. Phone the tenant when you arrive rather than knocking. There is a dog at the property and the tenant will take it out during the visit. Please check you have the tenant's contact number on the job. If you don't, reply and we will send it.

Scope for this visit:
- Upstairs bedroom Samsung TV: the tenant reports it trips the fuse/electrics when plugged in. It is unplugged at the moment. Please check it is safe and tell us what you find. Please don't repair, replace, remove or dispose of the TV. We are still confirming with the landlord whether it belongs to the property and what he wants done with it.
- Downstairs bedroom light: the tenant reports it flickers and pops when switched on. Please inspect it and tell us what is causing it. If a repair is needed, send us a quote with photos before you do any chargeable work. This item has not been approved by the landlord yet.
- If you find anything unsafe on the day, make it safe and tell us straight away.

Please send photos and a short report after the visit.

Many thanks,
Oren Pike
Maintenance Coordinator, Northbridge Lettings
decision.rationale: The latest real message (E019) is the electrician proposing 29 Sept after 15:00. The tenant offered exactly that slot in E016. What is missing is an arrival window and a confirmed booking, so the contractor needs a reply from us now. Landlord approval to attend for the TV is on record (E003 "Please sort it", recorded in E004). The light was added to the job afterwards (E005, E017) and the landlord has never approved it. He also doubted the TV is his ("I don't remember leaving a TV"), and nobody has put disposal to him, even though the tenant is open to the TV going (E015). So the visit can go ahead, but the contractor must not repair or dispose of the TV and must quote before any chargeable work on the light. The tenant hears the date in the same turn, with interim safety advice for the light and TV and a reminder about the rear-door handle (E015, E018). The landlord is told what is happening and asked the two scope questions. His auto-reply says he is away (E007), so we email now so the answer can arrive before the 29th. None of this needs escalating. A popping light the tenant has stopped using and a TV that is unplugged are risks to manage with safety advice. They are not an active hazard right now.
decision.expectedOutcome: The electrician confirms the 29 Sept booking with an arrival window, and agrees to phone on arrival and to the scope limits. The tenant confirms the slot. The landlord answers on the TV and the light before the visit.
boundaries: A proposed or booked slot does not mean the work is done.
This does not approve any repair or spend on the downstairs light. The electrician must quote first and the landlord must approve.
This does not decide who owns the TV and does not authorise repairing, removing or disposing of it.
The tenant's view that the main board is fried is not a diagnosis.
Sending the email does not mean the electrician has read it or agreed to the arrival window.

After the visit: findings, photos, any quotes to the landlord, then evidence, invoice and landlord update.

Oren Pike

final.rationale: The latest real message (E019) is the electrician proposing 29 Sept after 15:00. The tenant offered exactly that slot in E016. What is missing is an arrival window and a confirmed booking, so the contractor needs a reply from us now. Landlord approval to attend for the TV is on record (E003 "Please sort it", recorded in E004). The light was added to the job afterwards (E005, E017) and the landlord has never approved it. He also doubted the TV is his ("I don't remember leaving a TV"), and nobody has put disposal to him, even though the tenant is open to the TV going (E015). So the visit can go ahead, but the contractor must not repair or dispose of the TV and must quote before any chargeable work on the light. The tenant hears the date in the same turn, with interim safety advice for the light and TV and a reminder about the rear-door handle (E015, E018). The landlord is told what is happening and asked the two scope questions. His auto-reply says he is away (E007), so we email now so the answer can arrive before the 29th. None of this needs escalating. A popping light the tenant has stopped using and a TV that is unplugged are risks to manage with safety advice. They are not an active hazard right now.
final.expectedOutcome: The electrician confirms the 29 Sept booking with an arrival window, and agrees to phone on arrival and to the scope limits. The tenant confirms the slot. The landlord answers on the TV and the light before the visit.
boundaries: A proposed or booked slot does not mean the work is done.
This does not approve any repair or spend on the downstairs light. The electrician must quote first and the landlord must approve.
This does not decide who owns the TV and does not authorise repairing, removing or disposing of it.
The tenant's view that the main board is fried is not a diagnosis.
Sending the email does not mean the electrician has read it or agreed to the arrival window.
remainingWork: Get the electrician's arrival window and booking confirmation, and chase on 19 Sept if nothing arrives.
Get the tenant's confirmation of 29 Sept and relay the arrival window to her.

Get the landlord's decision on TV ownership and repair/disposal, and his approval or refusal for the light. If he has not replied by about 22 Sept, chase by another channel or ask the property manager to.
Rear-door handle: wait for the tenant's separate report and raise it as a new job. Check whether the door still locks.
After the visit: findings, photos, any quotes to the landlord, then evidence, invoice and landlord update.
